provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Primary one readiness
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to copy longer passages.
The pupils should be able to build writing stamina.

Introduction:
We have learned to write short words.
Today we write more words without stopping.

Content:
We copy passages from the board.
We write for five minutes without rest.
We use our best handwriting.
We write about our school and family.

Class activity:
Pupils will copy a short paragraph about their favourite food.

Evaluation questions:
Can you copy this passage?
How long can you write without stopping?
What makes good handwriting?

Summary:
We are ready for primary one writing tasks.

topics.title: Note taking start
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to write simple notes.
The pupils should be able to follow spoken steps.

Introduction:
We listen to our teacher every day.
Today we write down what we hear.

Content:
We write in short sentences.
We use bullet points for steps.
We write numbers in order.
We write about how to make tea.

Class activity:
Teacher gives steps for washing hands.
Pupils write the steps in order.

Evaluation questions:
What is note taking?
How do we write steps?
Can you write three steps for brushing teeth?

Summary:
Note taking helps us remember important things.

topics.title: Composition mastery
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to write five sentences.
The pupils should be able to plan a simple composition.

Introduction:
We have written many words and sentences.
Today we write about our graduation day.

Content:
We think about graduation first.
We write five sentences about it.
We start with when and where.
We write about what we will wear.
We end with how we feel.

Class activity:
Pupils draw graduation pictures.
Then write five sentences about their drawing.

Evaluation questions:
How many sentences in your composition?
What will you wear to graduation?
Why is graduation important?

Summary:
We can now write short compositions about events.

topics.title: Story with pictures
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to illustrate a story.
The pupils should be able to write author and illustrator names.

Introduction:
We love story time with pictures.
Today we make our own story with pictures.

Content:
We think of a simple story.
We draw pictures for each part.
We write the story under the pictures.
We write our name as author.
We write our name as illustrator.

Class activity:
Pupils create a story about a lost cat.
They draw three pictures and write short sentences.

Evaluation questions:
Who is the author of your story?
Who is the illustrator of your story?
What makes a good story picture?

Summary:
We can now create our own illustrated stories.

topics.title: Spelling bee prep
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to spell word lists.
The pupils should be able to participate in a spelling bee.

Introduction:
We know many words and their sounds.
Today we learn to spell them correctly.

Content:
We practice spelling common words.
We play spelling games in class.
We spell words like cat, dog, sun.
We spell days of the week.
We have a class spelling bee.

Class activity:
Teacher calls out words one by one.
Pupils spell them aloud correctly.

Evaluation questions:
Can you spell Monday?
What is your favorite spelling game?
How do you spell your name?

Summary:
We are ready for the spelling bee competition.

topics.title: Handwriting olympics
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to write neatly and quickly.
The pupils should be able to write with pride.

Introduction:
We practice handwriting every day.
Today we have a handwriting competition.

Content:
We write as neatly as we can.
We write as fast as we can.
We write with pride and confidence.
We write the alphabet in capital letters.
We write numbers from one to twenty.

Class activity:
Pupils write a sentence in two minutes.
The teacher checks for neatness and speed.

Evaluation questions:
What makes good handwriting?
How can you write faster?
Why is neat handwriting important?

Summary:
We are handwriting champions in our class.

topics.title: Autograph pages
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to write in friends' memory books.
The pupils should be able to practice their signature.

Introduction:
We have made many friends in school.
Today we write nice messages for them.

Content:
We write our name nicely in books.
We write short messages like good luck.
We draw small pictures next to words.
We practice writing our signature.
We use different colored pens.

Class activity:
Pupils exchange memory books.
They write their name and a message for each friend.

Evaluation questions:
What is an autograph?
Why do we write in memory books?
How do you write your signature?

Summary:
We can now write nice messages for our friends.

topics.title: Graduation programme copy
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to copy programme lines.
The pupils should be able to contribute to graduation day.

Introduction:
Our graduation day is coming soon.
Today we practice writing for the programme.

Content:
We copy lines from the graduation programme.
We write our part in the programme.
We write clearly and carefully.
We practice saying our lines while writing.
We feel proud of our writing.

Class activity:
Pupils copy their graduation programme lines neatly.
Then practice saying them aloud.

Evaluation questions:
What will you say at graduation?
Why is copying important for the programme?
How does writing help in graduation?

Summary:
We are ready for our graduation performance.

topics.title: Final portfolio page
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to select their proudest writing.
The pupils should be able to mount writing for graduation.

Introduction:
We have done much writing this term.
Today we choose our best work to show.

Content:
 We look at all our writing.
 We pick the one we like most.
 We write why we like it.
 We mount it on colored paper.
 We show it to our parents.

Class activity:
Pupils select their best writing and mount it.
They share it with a partner and explain why they chose it.

Evaluation questions:
Which writing did you pick?
Why is it your best work?
How do you mount your writing nicely?

Summary:
We have created our final portfolio page.

topics.title: Revision and send off
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to review their writing journey.
The pupils should be able to write about going to primary one.

Introduction:
We have learned so much this term.
Today we remember our writing journey.

Content:
We look at all our handwriting work.
We remember how we started.
We write about going to primary one.
We write what we will do there.
We feel proud and excited.

Class activity:
Pupils write a short message to their future primary one teacher.
They draw a picture of themselves in primary one uniform.

Evaluation questions:
What did you learn in handwriting?
How do you feel about primary one?
What will you do differently in primary one?

Summary:
We are ready for primary one and excited to learn more.
